 Toyota's Hybrid Minivan Gets Recalls, 228K Sienna People Carriers Affected Stateside
 The seatbelt pretensioners can trigger enough movement to unlock the seat backs during certain frontal crash scenarios, increasing the risk of injury 
 Published: 2 Nov 2026, 13:23 UTC 
 By: 
 Mircea Panait 
   14 photos Photo: Toyota / edited 
 In the world of automotive seatbelts, the pretensioner has one clear job, and that is to pull the belt tight during a crash. This keeps the occupant in place, minimizing the risk of injury. As far as certain Sienna hybrids are concerned, that pull can make the second-row seat recliner mechanism oscillate until its locking mechanism disengages. 
 This concern prompted a recall totaling 228,367 vehicles in the US market, namely Sienna minivans produced for model years 2022 through 2026. For North America, the Sienna is proudly assembled by Toyota Motor Manufacturing Indiana on the GA-K platform that underpins the Highlander twins. Over in China, two joint ventures produce the Sienna in Guangzhou and Tianjin, respectively.
 Regarding the US-market recall population, the failure requires a specific combination of pretensioner timing, seat back movement, and frontal crash forces for the second-row seats to fold when they should not. Toyota identified this combination while investigating seat assemblies, reproducing the condition as part of internal crash testing.
 Although the pretensioner does exactly what it's expected to do, the forces it generates can interfere with the mechanism that holds the seat back upright. Each second-row seat has an integrated seatbelt and pretensioner, and said pretensioner is designed to retract the belt in the event of a crash. The seat back, meanwhile, uses an outboard recliner mechanism with interlocking teeth.
 When the pretensioner deploys, the load from its deployment creates oscillation between the recliner's cam and pawls. In combination with relative seat back displacement, pretensioner deployment timing, and frontal crash pulses, the cam may rotate far enough to disengage the recliner from the locked position. This, in turn, allows the seat back to move during a crash.
 Photo: Toyota 
TMNA started looking into this matter back in January 2025, when a modified seat assembly and a modified seatbelt assembly were tested for a future production-intent model. During sled tests, the outboard recliner disengaged. Through August 2026, the company ran additional tests to isolate the variables. Toyota Motor North America further recovered second-row seat assemblies from the field to check the condition of the recliners.
 Full vehicle crash tests followed suit between September and October 2026, and those crash tests helped Toyota reproduce the conditions it had previously identified on the sled. Internally referred to as 26V690 by the NHTSA , this recall comprises Sienna hybrids assembled from September 16, 2021, through July 20, 2026.
 Toyota Boshoku Indiana is listed in the recall documentation as the seat assembly supplier. The remedy splits the recall population into two groups. For approximately 200 units equipped with the Mobility as a Service Package, both second-row seat backs will be replaced in full. The replacements feature a different recliner mechanism.
 The remaining vehicle population will be fixed through software, with Toyota instructing dealers to install updated SRS electronic control unit software. Known customers will be notified by first-class mail no later than December 21, 2026.
